description: Run the full deterministic L1 code-vetting pipeline over a target tree and return a bounded metrics summary plus a severity-ranked markdown report. Default (no 'target_path') is a self-vet of the platform's own git worktree, byte-compatible with the prior behavior. An optional ABSOLUTE 'target_path' vets a FOREIGN repo/source tree instead, READ-ONLY (the engine never writes into the target): validated fail-loud (absolute, exists, is a directory, must not resolve inside our own worktree), enumerated git-preferred (the target's own 'git ls-files') with a structural walk fallback for a non-git tree (curated excludes, NO gitignore emulation), with the derived target_class + enumeration mode + detected language stacks + file count recorded. Runs all 20 scanners synchronously (secrets, SAST, dependency/license, the platform quality-gate wrappers, the identity/PII/network regex battery, hidden-unicode, duplication, orphan-KB, a multi-language structural-metrics scanner, an opt-in foreign-Python type-check scanner that runs the target's own configured pyright/mypy, and a self-only rulebook-integrity check) with no inference — on a foreign target the platform-local scanners (code_quality/sql_access/orphan_kb/prior_pass/rulebook_sync) skip execution but stay in the coverage ledger as not_applicable so the roster never shrinks, and stack-gated scanners record not_applicable when their language stack is absent. The structural-metrics scanner (lizard, parse-only, every language) reports per-function complexity/length/parameter/nesting-depth distributions in a dedicated report section on EVERY run; it is report-not-gate, emitting band-crossing findings (complexity dimension, severity ceiling MEDIUM) only on foreign targets and suppressing those rows on a self-vet where the commit gates already own that surface. Two of the scanners are the TARGET's own toolchain — tsc (strict TypeScript typecheck) and eslint — which run ONLY on TS/JS targets AND only when the caller sets 'execute_target_toolchain' (default false), because they EXECUTE TARGET-CONTROLLED CODE (config JS, plugins, and node_modules/.bin binaries) on the scan host; prefer the Phase-2 sandbox, on-host execution is a discouraged flagged escape hatch — without the opt-in (or a materialized node_modules) they record a coverage gap rather than running. The same 'execute_target_toolchain' opt-in also gates the foreign-Python type-check scanner (pyright/mypy), which runs the target's OWN declared type-check configuration against its existing {.venv,venv} environment (the engine never installs or creates a venv); with no such config it records a distinct 'no static-typing contract' gap, and on a self-vet its finding rows are suppressed (the platform pyright --strict gate stays sole self authority). The self-only rulebook-integrity scanner (rulebook_sync) verifies the shipped assembled AI-critic rulebook still matches its committed hash manifest AND has not drifted behind its sources, emitting a HIGH code_quality 'stale_rulebook' finding plus a report integrity banner when the moat is stale or corrupt (self-policing so a stale moat never silently seeds the AI-critic pass). Optional 'scope' is a cosmetic label. Optional 'persist' (default false) writes this run to the vetting_runs trail as a side-effect so get_vetting_run can read it back by run_id (the joseki's payload-by-run_id seam) — the returned payload is byte-identical whether or not it persists, and a persisted L1-only run is recorded under substrate 'heuristic' (no inference), bounded by the same retention as the driver's trail. The minutes-long AI-critic (L2) and adversarial-verify (L3) stages are NOT part of this verb — they run as joseki-dispatched agent sessions.
embedding_description: Run the whole deterministic security-and-quality vetting suite over the codebase: every L1 scanner at once — leaked-secret detection, static application security analysis, vulnerable-dependency and license checks, the platform quality gates, an operator-identity/PII/network-bind regex battery, hidden-unicode, code duplication, and orphaned knowledge-base detection — returning finding counts by severity and dimension, coverage gaps, and a ranked markdown report. This is the broad full-suite scan; it does NOT run AI critics or inference. Use it for a complete deterministic vet of the repository, not a narrow quality-gate-only check.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Object: run_id, target ({repo, ref, scope} — ref is empty in walk-enumeration mode), target_class ('self' or 'foreign'), enumeration ('git' or 'walk'), files_enumerated (int), stacks (detected language stacks — a subset of python/typescript/javascript — the engine's provenance for what the target is; gates the stack-specific scanners), started/finished ISO timestamps, total_findings, counts_by_severity (blocker/high/medium/low/advisory), counts_by_dimension, scanners_ran, scanners_total (the full roster; a foreign run's platform-local scanners are not_applicable, and stack-gated scanners are not_applicable when their language stack is absent — counted in the coverage but not run), coverage_gaps (scanners that could not run, with reason — 'not_applicable:' for platform-local or stack-absent scanners, distinct from a tool-missing gap; the target-toolchain scanners tsc/eslint and the foreign-Python type-check scanner record an opt-in gap unless 'execute_target_toolchain' is set and the target's env (node_modules / {.venv,venv}) is present, plus a distinct 'no static-typing contract' gap when a Python target declares no pyright/mypy config), and report (a bounded severity-ranked markdown register with a '## Structural Quality Metrics' section — multi-language complexity distributions + worst-offenders + a repeated-literal subsection (magic-string/value candidates, evidence-only) — and a '## Candidate Dead Symbols' section (unused functions/classes/methods/variables at 60% confidence from the in-process vulture scanner — evidence for the AI-critic layer, NOT findings; the provable dead-code classes unreachable-code and unused-import render as normal finding cards), truncation-marked if it exceeds the cap). The per-run structural-metrics distribution and the candidate-dead-symbols list are also persisted to the vetting_runs trend + L2-targeting trail.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with the headline: total_findings and the severity histogram (blocker/high first). Name any coverage_gaps explicitly — a gap means a tool was absent or a scanner was not applicable, not that the code is clean. On a TS/JS target, tsc/eslint showing an opt-in gap is the DEFAULT (target-toolchain execution is off unless the caller opts in) — not a failure. Offer the markdown report for the finding detail. Note the run is a deterministic scan (minutes for the full toolchain), not an AI review; the AI-critic pass is a separate joseki.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Running the deterministic L1 code-vetting suite over the local git worktree.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: invalid_target_path: the supplied 'target_path' failed a fail-loud validation check — the message names which (not absolute / does not exist / not a directory / resolves inside or around the platform's own worktree, where self-vet is the default). A RuntimeError about locating the worktree root means the verb could not find an ancestor of APP_HOME carrying both quality_gates/ and .git — the self-vet path is local-profile only and requires the git worktree (a cloud homunculus has none). A git failure from TargetTree means a git-mode target is not a readable git repo. An unexpected scanner exception is a real defect (the scanners convert expected tool-absence into coverage gaps, so a raised exception is not a normal condition).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: invalid_target_path: fix the named check — pass an absolute path to an existing external directory that is NOT inside our own worktree (omit target_path entirely to self-vet our own tree). Confirm the homunculus runs on a local profile whose APP_HOME sits under the git worktree for a self-vet (this plugin is excluded from cloud manifests by design). If a specific scanner raised, treat it as a bug in that scanner rather than retrying blindly.
